stem.en: International business refers to:

options.en: trade between two states of the same country
manufacturing and trade activities that cross national frontiers
business done only by the government

explanation.en: International business includes all business activities across national borders, not only trade.

stem.en: The basic reason for international business is that:

options.en: all countries produce every good at the same cost
all goods are equally available everywhere
nations differ in natural resources and in costs of production

explanation.en: Unequal resources and differences in productivity and costs lead to specialisation and trade.

stem.en: Which of the following is a feature of international business but NOT of domestic business?

options.en: Transactions involve more than one currency
Buyers and sellers belong to the same country
One uniform set of laws applies

explanation.en: International transactions involve different currencies and exchange rate risk.

stem.en: Factors of production such as labour and capital are generally:

options.en: more mobile between countries than within a country
less mobile between countries than within a country

explanation.en: Laws on immigration, investment and currency restrict mobility across national borders.

stem.en: Trade in services such as tourism, banking and insurance is also called:

explanation.en: Services are intangible, so their trade is called invisible trade.

stem.en: An investor buys shares of a foreign company only to earn dividends, without any control over it. This is:

explanation.en: Portfolio investment gives income but no control; direct investment involves control.

stem.en: Which is a benefit of international business to a nation?

options.en: Earning foreign exchange to pay for imports

explanation.en: Exports earn foreign exchange that is used to import capital goods, technology and other necessities.

stem.en: A firm facing intense competition at home enters foreign markets. Which benefit to firms does this show?

options.en: Earning of foreign exchange for the nation
A way out of intense competition in the domestic market
Efficient use of the nation's resources

explanation.en: International markets offer firms an escape from saturated or highly competitive home markets.

stem.en: The easiest way of entering international markets, with the least investment and risk, is:

explanation.en: Exporting needs little investment and involvement compared with other modes.

stem.en: Under licensing, the fee paid by the licensee to the licensor is called:

explanation.en: The licensee pays a royalty for the right to use patents, trademarks or know-how.

stem.en: In a wholly owned subsidiary, the parent company holds:

options.en: 100% of the equity capital of the foreign company
only a contract to buy goods

explanation.en: A wholly owned subsidiary is fully owned and controlled by the parent company.

stem.en: Franchising differs from licensing mainly because franchising is used for:

options.en: service businesses, with the franchisee following a strict business format

explanation.en: Franchising is a special form of licensing for services, with tighter control over the business format.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Exporting is the simplest mode of entry into international business.
Reason (R): Exporting needs far less investment than setting up a wholly owned subsidiary abroad.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both true; low investment and involvement are why exporting is the simplest mode.

stem.en: Option 3 is an example of a:

explanation.en: A new firm owned jointly by two independent firms is a joint venture.

passage.en: Nandi Foods, a Karnataka snack maker, wants to enter the UAE market. Option 1: ship packed snacks to a Dubai distributor. Option 2: allow a Dubai firm to make and sell the snacks under the Nandi brand using Nandi's recipe, paying 4% of sales. Option 3: set up a new company in Dubai with a local partner, each owning half. The directors want low risk now, but full control later.

stem.en: To get full control later, Nandi Foods should finally move to:

explanation.en: Only a wholly owned subsidiary (100% equity) gives full control.

passage.en: Nandi Foods, a Karnataka snack maker, wants to enter the UAE market. Option 1: ship packed snacks to a Dubai distributor. Option 2: allow a Dubai firm to make and sell the snacks under the Nandi brand using Nandi's recipe, paying 4% of sales. Option 3: set up a new company in Dubai with a local partner, each owning half. The directors want low risk now, but full control later.

stem.en: The document on the basis of which customs gives permission for export is the:

explanation.en: The exporter files the shipping bill for customs clearance of exports.

stem.en: A bill of lading is issued by:

explanation.en: The shipping company issues the bill of lading as receipt for goods on board and document of title.

stem.en: The document issued by the commanding officer of a ship when the goods are loaded on board is the:

explanation.en: The mate's receipt is issued by the ship's officer and later exchanged for the bill of lading.

stem.en: Under documents against acceptance (D/A), the importer gets the shipping documents:

options.en: only after making full payment immediately
before the exporter ships the goods
without any bill of exchange at all
on accepting a usance bill of exchange, with payment due later

explanation.en: D/A uses a usance (time) draft; D/P uses a sight draft and needs immediate payment.

stem.en: A guarantee issued by the importer's bank that it will honour payment up to a certain amount of export bills is a:

explanation.en: The letter of credit assures the exporter of payment by the importer's bank.

stem.en: The document filed by an importer for assessment of customs duty and clearance of imported goods is the:

explanation.en: The bill of entry is the importer's customs document; the shipping bill is the exporter's.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The bill of lading is issued by the customs authorities.
Reason (R): The bill of lading serves as a document of title to the goods.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is false: the shipping company issues the bill of lading. R is true: it is a document of title.

stem.en: Under the duty drawback scheme:

options.en: duties paid on goods or inputs that are exported are refunded to the exporter
imports of consumer goods are banned
the exporter is given land free of cost

explanation.en: Duty drawback refunds customs and excise duties paid on exported goods or their inputs.

stem.en: Which organisation provides insurance to exporters against the risk of non-payment by foreign buyers?

explanation.en: ECGC covers exporters against commercial and political risks of non-payment.

stem.en: The World Trade Organisation came into existence on:

explanation.en: The WTO replaced GATT on 1 January 1995.

stem.en: Which of the following is a function of the WTO?

options.en: Collecting income tax in member countries
Settling trade disputes between member countries
Fixing the retail price of goods within a country

explanation.en: Dispute settlement, administering trade agreements and reviewing trade policies are WTO functions.

stem.en:
Assertion (A): The duty drawback scheme makes Indian exports more competitive.
Reason (R): Under this scheme, duties paid on exported goods or their inputs are refunded.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: Both are true, and R explains A: refunding duties lowers the cost of exported goods.
